q1.question: Is there a minimum contract?
q1.answer: The first cycle is 6 months. That's the time we need to calibrate the partnership, understand your operation's rhythm and deliver real value. After that, no lock-in — just 30 days' notice to organize the transition.

q2.question: What happens to unused hours at the end of the month?
q2.answer: Hours don't roll over. We work with limited, controlled capacity — if they did, we'd lose the quality control that's exactly what you're paying for. In the last week of the month we accept no more than 25% of the total package, precisely to avoid end-of-month rushes.

q3.question: What if I have an urgent issue outside business hours?
q3.answer: An emergency is an emergency — reach out anytime. But it's worth knowing our process is designed to minimize emergencies: we don't make store changes after 3pm on weekdays or at any time on Fridays, to protect the weekend. If something happens outside that, we'll be online as soon as possible.

q4.question: My previous agency didn't hand over the code. Can you take over?
q4.answer: For Continuous Evolution, we prefer not to take on projects without code history — in some cases, like VTEX IO, it's not even technically possible. But if that's your situation, we can build a new project from scratch. With one advantage: the code is yours, guaranteed in the contract. If you ever decide to move on — though we doubt you'll want to — you take everything with you.

q5.question: How do I request work?
q5.answer: We work with Monday.com. Each partner has their own board, with access for up to 3 people from your team — to create, prioritize and validate the tasks to be executed.

q6.question: How do I reach you for a quick question?
q6.answer: Each partner has a WhatsApp group with us — the channel for urgent matters and quick questions. Anything that makes sense as a task, we move to Monday.

q7.question: Do you handle product registration?
q7.answer: We don't handle product registration directly — the operational details stay with you, and we don't want to risk inconsistencies in your product data. But we provide full support: guidance, documentation, and when needed, a call to do assisted registration with your team.

q8.question: If I have more than one store, do I need two contracts?
q8.answer: No. You sign one contract with us and we can cover all your stores — as long as they're on the platforms we work with. You decide how to best distribute the hours between them.

q9.question: Are SEO and performance included in the plan or billed separately?
q9.answer: Technical SEO and performance are part of the standard flow — included in the regular plan. GEO is a separate product, as it requires analysis, documentation and ongoing monitoring that goes beyond the day-to-day of the store.

q10.question: Do you do in-person meetings?
q10.answer: We're nomadic, so we have the freedom to be in many places. If we're in your city at the right time, it'll be a pleasure. If not, we can align travel costs and schedule something — freedom is never in short supply.

q11.question: Do you only execute, or do you also analyze and suggest?
q11.answer: We prefer doing the full work — analyzing, bringing ideas, thinking together, spotting opportunities. But we respect each partner's rhythm. If your strategy team already calls all the shots, we execute with quality. If you want us involved in the decisions and a technical eye on the strategy — even better.

q12.question: Is there a monthly alignment meeting?
q12.answer: Yes. In the first week of every month we have a fixed meeting with each partner — set at kick-off — to talk about where the store stands, planned actions and brainstorm for the next cycle.

q13.question: How do I track my hours balance?
q13.answer: Inside Monday you have access to a custom dashboard with all activities, hours and status of everything executed throughout the year — month by month, in real time.

q14.question: What platforms do you work with?
q14.answer: We work with VTEX and Nuvemshop. The platform choice depends on the moment, the volume and the brand's strategy — and it's part of what we assess together with the client when needed.

q1.question: What is GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)?
q1.answer: GEO is the practice of optimizing your site and content to appear in AI-generated responses from tools like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity. Unlike traditional SEO, which focuses on ranking pages in search engines, GEO focuses on ensuring AIs know, understand and cite your brand in the responses they generate.

q2.question: What's the difference between SEO and GEO?
q2.answer: SEO is optimization for traditional search engines like Google, which return a list of links. GEO is optimization for generative search engines — AIs that return answers directly. Good technical SEO is the foundation of GEO, but GEO goes further: it requires structured content, citable statements, brand authority and structured data that language models can process.

q3.question: Is the free audit really free?
q3.answer: Yes, 100% free and no commitment. You provide your site URL and email, and receive a full report with GEO Readiness score, technical SEO score, identified gaps and prioritized action plan. No credit card or sensitive data required.

q4.question: What platforms does the audit work for?
q4.answer: The GEO Audit works for any website or e-commerce, regardless of platform — VTEX, Nuvemshop, WooCommerce, Magento or any other. The analysis is done on your site's public URL, checking the technical and content signals used by AI crawlers.

q5.question: How quickly will I get the results?
q5.answer: The report is generated in under 60 seconds and sent to the email you provide. You can also access the results directly on the page after analysis.

q6.question: What is the GEO Checker and how does it work?
q6.answer: The GEO Checker is dup.agency's complete product for monitoring AI presence. Unlike the Audit (which analyzes your site's technical potential), the Checker verifies in practice whether your site is already being mentioned in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity responses for questions in your niche. It's an ongoing monitoring and reporting service.

problems.headline: Your sitemap has errors Google is already penalizing you for.

p1.title: Unnecessary redirects
p1.body: Every redirect is an extra instruction for Google. Long chains dilute PageRank and increase response time.

p2.title: 404 errors
p2.body: Dead URLs in the sitemap confuse the crawler and signal technical negligence to search engines.

p3.title: Redirect loops
p3.body: When A points to B and B points to A, the crawler gives up. Your page disappears from the index.

p4.title: Slow URLs
p4.body: Pages above 3s TTFB are deprioritized in crawling. Speed is an indexing criterion.

problems.body: A sitemap with unnecessary redirects, URLs returning 404, redirect loops or slow pages pollutes the Google index and wastes crawl budget — without you noticing.

q1.question: What is crawl budget and why does it matter?
q1.answer: Crawl budget is the number of pages Googlebot is willing to crawl on your site in a given period. Sites with many redirects, 404s or duplicate URLs waste this budget — and important pages may go uncrawled.

q2.question: Do I need to install anything?
q2.answer: No. The tool accesses your sitemap.xml publicly, the same way Google does. No access, plugins or credentials required.

q3.question: What platforms does it work for?
q3.answer: Works for any platform — VTEX, Nuvemshop, WooCommerce or any other CMS that generates a public sitemap.xml.

q4.question: What do I do after receiving the report?
q4.answer: The report already comes with recommended actions by priority. If you want dup.agency to execute the fixes, just get in touch — most identified issues are resolved in a single sprint.

q5.question: How often should I run the audit?
q5.answer: We recommend running it after any major URL change (migration, category restructuring, new sitemap) and at least once per quarter as a routine check.
